title: Learned correction improves retrospective infliximab concentration estimates in young patients
summary: XGBoost corrected errors from a population-pharmacokinetic Bayesian model using measured infliximab concentrations in young patients with Crohn’s disease. Internal cross-validation reduced concentration prediction error, but some cases worsened and no external or prospective treatment-benefit evaluation was shown. The result concerns measured drug concentrations, without established improvements in dosing safety or disease outcomes.
ai_technology: XGBoost error correction integrated with population-pharmacokinetic Bayesian estimation
organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; University of Cincinnati; Connecticut Children’s Medical Center; Nationwide Children’s Hospital; Children’s Hospital of Wisconsin

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 292 successive-concentration pairs from 93 patients aged 2–22 years. XGBoost learned prediction errors using clinical features and prior drug measurements. Five-fold evaluation reported RMSE 3.78 ± 0.85 micrograms/mL versus 4.8 for Bayesian estimation alone. Absolute error improved modestly on average; the source also reports worsened predictions in a subset.
evidence.unknown: Multiple observations per patient were present, but explicit patient-grouped folds were not established in the reviewed Methods. Correlation-based feature selection and algorithm comparisons may affect internal performance; independent final evaluation was absent. Low concentrations below quantification were excluded. This is retrospective evaluation, without demonstrated clinical remission, safety improvement or validated continuous-learning deployment.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost learned residual prediction patterns and adjusted the prior pharmacokinetic estimates; comparison with measured subsequent concentrations supplies the specific clinical validation result. The pre-existing Bayesian model/dashboard alone is not treated as a new discovery.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical cohort/consecutive-concentration design, Bayesian and XGBoost residual-learning/tuning/evaluation Methods, measured-concentration error Results and limitations. Patient-grouped fold independence and supplementary implementation were not established; dosing procedures or clinical recommendations not represented. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
